pr_title: Shift to yaml v3 and fix duplicate errors in Promtool
pr_body:
<!--
    Don't forget!
    
    - If the PR adds or changes a behaviour or fixes a bug of an exported API it would need a unit/e2e test.
    
    - Where possible use only exported APIs for tests to simplify the review and make it as close as possible to an actual library usage.
    
    - No tests are needed for internal implementation changes.
    
    - Performance improvements would need a benchmark test to prove it.
    
    - All exposed objects should have a comment.
    
    - All comments should start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
 -->

Fixes: #7042 
Fixes: #7128 

Improvements:
1. (Fixed by another PR as well) The reported issue of labels parsing error being skipped is fixed. Hence,
```
groups:
  - name: group
    rules:
      - alert: alert
        expr: expr
        labels:
          key : value
        foo: bar
```

will result to

```
[hsingh@localhost prometheus]$ ./promtool check rules rule.yml 
Checking rule.yml
  FAILED:
rule.yml: yaml: unmarshal errors:
  line 8: field foo not found in type rulefmt.Rule
```

2. Duplicate errors in the previous version related to yaml unmarshalling is fixed.
3. Shift to yaml v3 library across the application.
pr_comments: /cc @brian-brazil @roidelapluie
@brian-brazil What do you think about this?
I still think that we should not be importing two different YAML library versions, and should instead be fixing our usage of the existing library.
I agree with @brian-brazil seems like the addition of yaml.v3 has introduced a number of regressions.
@brian-brazil I think we have some after this [comment](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml/issues/602#issuecomment-623485602).
Let's update our usage then to fix the regression.
@brian-brazil we can move ahead in this now. Thank you for the suggestions @roidelapluie.
@roidelapluie implemented the changes from #7208. Please have a look.
@roidelapluie done!
@brian-brazil @roidelapluie should we move ahead.
Tests are failing
@roidelapluie fixed! No idea on the failing ones like windows and the fuzzing. Seems like system issues.
@brian-brazil @roidelapluie cc
@brian-brazil can we move ahead?
@brian-brazil cc
@brian-brazil I think we can go ahead with the merge if everything seems fine to us.

Essentially our worry is that we have sooo many Rules structs. For API, For internal use, For yaml parsing and for UI. Now for yaml parsing we have 2 which is crazy.

In comparison in Thanos we have just one: which is capable to parse to many different things (including protobuf itself), all done from proto: https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/714ac05388615da8a37b1cc50d916cd90509ac1f/pkg/rules/rulespb/rpc.proto#L67

This means we can do much better here in Prometheus.

@bwplotka the point is that if we marshal any struct that contains a `yaml.Node`, we get additional details like `linecomment`, `headcomment`, etc, which looks messy and unnecessary for the purpose of showing in the view. Thats the reason we need to have at least 2 structs, First, for features for promtool, Second, for views.

I can convert the anonymous types to a defined one, but that would be along with `rulefmt.Rule`, like `rulefmt.RuleTempl` or something around that. If that does not sound good, please give some suggestions on how to have within a single struct. @brian-brazil @bwplotka

> Thats the reason we need to have at least 2 structs, First, for features for promtool, Second, for views.

If yaml v3 can't do such marshalling without duplicating all of our config structs, we either need to learn how to do it, get it added upstream, or abandon v3.
By referencing nodes as pointers, that might be possible, but I think that will also involve few changes in other files as well.

> > Thats the reason we need to have at least 2 structs, First, for features for promtool, Second, for views.
> 
> If yaml v3 can't do such marshalling without duplicating all of our config structs, we either need to learn how to do it, get it added upstream, or abandon v3.

It can do without duplicate but in this case duplicate is needed to get the exact line / position in the file.

> It can do without duplicate but in this case duplicate is needed to get the exact line / position in the file.

My point is that we'd ultimately want to be on v3 everywhere, and if we need to duplicate the entirety of prometheus.yml just to show it on the status page then I question if v3 is worth it. This seems like a usage/feature issue with v3 which we should resolve.

Couldn't this pull request be limited to:

```
diff --git a/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go b/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go
index 1d6716beb..804c05352 100644
--- a/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go
+++ b/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go
@@ -14,6 +14,7 @@
 package rulefmt
 
 import (
+       "bytes"
        "context"
        "io/ioutil"
        "strings"
@@ -267,7 +268,9 @@ func Parse(content []byte) (*RuleGroups, []error) {
                errs   []error
        )
 
-       err := yaml.Unmarshal(content, &groups)
+       decoder := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(content))
+       decoder.KnownFields(true)
+       err := decoder.Decode(&groups)
        if err != nil {
                errs = append(errs, err)
        }
```

> Couldn't this pull request be limited to:

I think, that might fail the tests that involve HTML outputs. That's the reason why the anonymous structs are used.
Sorry for the delay on this. I was involved in #7779. Now that it seems almost on track, I will focus on things required to get this done.

@brian-brazil @bwplotka @gotjosh @roidelapluie  I have reduced and made this work with lesser structs. That seemed like the most important issue. With this, I think we can have another round of review.
@brian-brazil addressed the comments!
Tests still aren't happy, but only breaking on Windows for some odd reason for something that isn't platform specific.
There should be nothing platform specific in any of this code, so any issues like that need to be investigated rather than removing key tests.
@brian-brazil done!

> Can you update the commit description to what this PR is doing now?

I guess, only the duplicate errors thing. But, since this has been quite sometime around, I am updating this PR to shift from yaml.v2 to yaml.v3 throught the application completely in reliable terms.

> Can you update the commit description to what this PR is doing now?

Done!
@brian-brazil updated!
@abursavich You have played with yamlv3, would you want to help us reviewing this? :) Thanks :)

> @abursavich You have played with yamlv3, would you want to help us reviewing this? :) Thanks :)

Yeah, sure. I'll take a look at this today, but as recently as few weeks ago I would've said that v3 isn't ready yet.

When I was working on the config stuff, I upgraded everything to v3 thinking it might make things better, but it only created more problems. Sorry to show up out of nowhere and be a party pooper, but nothing has changed in the meantime. There are too many serious issues with v3 and there's a reason why a v3.0.0 release hasn't been tagged yet.

> Sorry to show up out of nowhere and be a party pooper, but nothing has changed in the meantime

Well I did ask for your opinion, so you do not pop up from nowhere. Thanks for your message, and indeed:

- v2 is still default branch of the upstream repository
- v3 has a list of issues in the bug tracker

Note that we had a bug in the rules (which use v3) that was there in 2.16 to 2.20 and then fixed in 2.21, because we did not introduce strict marshalling. I'd be very careful about using more v3.

Ahh, then I think it will be good to keep this PR open and wait for some stable release of YAML v3. Since there's only one place left, it will be soon to implement the changes as soon as a stable release of YAML v3 is out.

issue_context.title: RuleGroups.Validate(...) needs unexported struct ruleGroups as input
issue_context.body:
I'm trying to upgrade prometheus dep in thanos and I'm stuck with this:

```shell
$ make build
all modules verified
>> building binaries /Users/s.rabot/go/bin
 >   thanos
# github.com/thanos-io/thanos/cmd/thanos
cmd/thanos/check.go:88:29: not enough arguments in call to promRgs.Validate
	have ()
	want (rulefmt.ruleGroups)
```

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/51c824543bca2f25baa6596827cf4fad8f18dc2e/pkg/rulefmt/rulefmt.go#L66

cc @bwplotka
comments: Why you put issue on Prometheus for this? It's normal we will have build errors to fix.  We plan to upgrade deps after chunk iterator.

Because I thought there was little that could be done in thanos if prometheus does not export `ruleGroups` or adds a `NewruleGroups() ruleGroups` func.

Am I mistaken ?

I think it should be exported for non-thanos related reasons.
For example if I want to build a tool that manages alerts, and not implement my own validation logic, I can't.

I could do something like this:
```go
_, errs := rulefmt.Parse([]byte(definition)
```
Then errs would have elements of type `rulefmt.Error` which have `WrappedError` that has needed context, but all of it's fields are unexported..
Use of our internals by 3rd parties is unsupported, but we will generally accept PRs to make things public.

Let's move forward with this then... (: 

It's blocking https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/pull/2535
Are you still happy to continue this @sylr
@bwplotka I wish I could but I am pretty busy at the moment.
Actually the way forward is to get back to yaml.v2 as there are missing features in yaml.v3
Do you have any details / related discussion @roidelapluie ?
Actually things are moving now.. I will see that later on.
cmd/thanos/check.go > I do not see that file in thanos codebase?

It just changed - it is now in cmd/thanos/tools.go
